content.title: View stored High or Low priority badge on a task card
content.intent: Prove that a task with an explicit stored priority shows that same allowed value on its badge for the non-default allowed values.
content.technique_notes: Equivalence partitioning across the explicit allowed priority values named in the PRD. Covered with covering_array over input stored_priority using requested strength=2 from low-risk, non-money, non-auth, non-data-loss behavior; tool degraded to effective strength=1 because there is only one input. No separate negative path was minted because the corpus does not specify invalid-priority handling or a way to create an invalid value through this use-case.

content.title: View Medium priority badge for a task with no explicit priority
content.intent: Prove that a task without an explicit priority displays the default Medium badge.
content.technique_notes: Happy-path scenario for the source-stated default behavior. Kept separate from explicit-value coverage because defaulting to Medium is a distinct outcome from rendering an already-stored explicit value.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applicable because the source defines a closed set of allowed displayed priority values: High, Medium, and Low. I used equivalence partitioning to separate the distinct default-Medium outcome from the explicit non-default High/Low outcomes.

[applicability] Not applicable for minting a scenario because the corpus states allowed values but does not define behavior for an invalid or unknown priority value, and this use-case exposes no editing flow that could create one.
[applicability] Not applicable because the source provides no ordered numeric range, length limit, or threshold for priority display behavior.
[applicability] Not applicable for a separate scenario because the source makes no accessibility promise about the priority badge; inventing one would not be faithful to the evidence.

[applicability] Not applicable for a separate scenario because the source only says the card layout stays as it is today, but the corpus provides no measurable responsive-layout baseline beyond preserved controls, which is already covered by invariant criteria.
[applicability] Not applicable because page reload persistence is a separate use-case in this corpus and is not part of the promised behavior of viewing task priority here.
